A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 40-page versions of the same work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, Appendices A-C, and checklist are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM experiments on deliberate versus incidental information, recommendation scenarios, and YouTube sponsorships, with quantitative results in Sections 3-5 and Appendices A-C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original LLM experiments and their quantitative outcomes, including the supplementary analyses in Appendices A-C.

M1.justification: The rational-model evaluation framework, elicitation procedures, and intentions-and-incentives steering intervention are unchanged. No algorithm, model component, or inference procedure is introduced or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same visual counting tasks, including diverse stimuli in A.5; credit-card, medicine, and real-estate scenarios; and 300 sampled YouTube sponsorships.

E2.justification: The evaluated LLMs, human reference data, Bayesian model comparisons, and alternative steering comparators remain identical. The newly cited work in Section 2.2 is not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Sections 3-5 and the appendices retain the same sample sizes, model configurations, prompting roles, temperatures, token limits, preprocessing, and evaluation metrics. No experimental setting or testing procedure changes.

E4.justification: The diverse-stimulus and initial-correctness checks in A.5-A.6, prompting and trust/incentive analyses in B.4-B.5, transcript-length comparison in Table 3, and alternative-steering analysis in C.2 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Repeated-run counts, plotted error bars, significance annotations, and statistical tests are unchanged, including the Fisher r-to-z comparisons in Section 5.4 and p-values in Table 4.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match across the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains GPT-4o's Bayesian-LLM correlation of 0.911, and Table 2 retains its direct-user default and steered correlations of -0.006 and 0.312.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same benevolence-weighted reward definition and speaker/listener equations (1)-(3). No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims: LLMs exhibit motivational vigilance in controlled settings, generalize less reliably to naturalistic sponsorships, and partially recover vigilance through steering.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning distracting context and increased salience of motivations remain unchanged. Section 6 also retains the same limitations concerning competence, broader sources of motivation, and generalization.

D1.justification: Prompt templates, image-noising and brand-censoring instructions, hyperparameters, and code/data-access statements are unchanged. Correcting a spelling error in A.4 adds no technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhao et al., 'Improving attributed long-form question answering with intent awareness,' as reference 101, supporting the existing Section 2.2 statement about misinterpreting communicative intent. Other works are retained, with subsequent references renumbered; research positioning is otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 corrects 'inclduing' to 'including' in A.4, removes a stray space after an em dash in Section 6, and updates citation numbering and the version/date stamp. The narrative and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-6 and Tables 1-7 are visually unchanged. The added citation causes local text reflow, and the added bibliography entry moves the WebArena reference from page 16 to page 17.

improvement.justification: The added Section 2.2 citation supports an already documented assertion, while spelling and spacing corrections provide slight editorial polish. Methods, empirical evidence, analyses, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, leaving no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
